items.question: I'll be picking my dog up after 5 hours. Is that a half day or a full day, and what does it cost?
items.why: A numeric limit: up to 4 hours is a half day, over 4 is a full day. The answer is right, but it opens with a needless "Yes,": the prompt asks for Yes or No on yes/no questions and this is an either/or question. A small flaw.
items.answer: Yes, picking up your dog after 5 hours is considered a full day, which costs $100.00. The pricing rules state that full day rates apply for stays over 4 hours, and half-day rates are for up to 4 hours. Since 5 hours exceeds the half-day limit, the full-day rate applies. Additionally, if pickup occurs after the facility's closing time (6:00 PM), a late fee may apply, but this question focuses on the duration, not the time of pickup.

items.question: My dog's rabies vaccination expired yesterday. Can I still bring him?
items.why: An exception (a 5-day grace period) that a plain yes or no would miss.
items.answer: Yes, you can still bring your dog, but only during the 5-day grace period. The dog cannot attend until updated proof of vaccination is received within this period. The rabies vaccination must be current, and the grace period applies to expired vaccinations. If the expiration date was yesterday, the 5-day grace period allows you to provide updated proof before the dog is denied entry.

passages.text: If a dog's vaccination expires, the dog cannot attend until updated proof is received. We do allow a grace period of 5 days.

Every dog must have current proof of the following vaccinations before their first visit:
- Rabies (valid for 3 years, depending on the vaccine given)
- DHPP, also called distemper/parvo (valid for 1 year after the booster series)
- Bordetella, also called kennel cough (must be given within the last 12 months)
- Canine influenza: recommended

Owners must send vaccination records from their veterinarian by email address,  in person or by online form. Records must show the dog's name, the vaccine, the date given, and the date it expires. Photos of paper records are not accepted.
Dogs must be on a flea and tick preventive. A dog found with fleas or ticks will be sent home and the owner will be notified.

items.question: Will you give my dog treats?
items.why: The documents only give a condition (treats need the owner's permission). A first version of the prompt made the model argue in circles over yes or no, sometimes for 38 minutes; the README tells that story.
items.answer: Treats are only given with owner permission.

items.question: Where do I wait at pick-up, and how many parking spaces are there?
items.why: Two facts on two pages of the PDF visitor guide. Open the passages to see the page numbers.
items.answer: At pick-up, wait at the lobby counter. There are 12 parking spaces in the lot behind the building.

passages.text:
Pick-up and Accessibility
Waiting at pick-up
At pick-up, wait at the lobby counter. Staff bring your dog out to you with the daily report. Please do
not go into the play areas yourself, even if you can see your dog through the gate.
Greeting other dogs
Keep your dog on a leash in the lobby. Please ask the other owner before you let your dog greet
another dog, and give shy dogs plenty of room.
Accessibility
The lobby, the side door and the restroom have no steps. A ramp leads up from the parking lot, and
the lobby counter has a lowered section for wheelchair users.

Barks n Woofs: Visitor Guide
Finding us
Barks n Woofs is at 123 puppy drive, Oakland ME. Look for the green awning. The front door is for
visitors. Dogs being dropped off or picked up use the side door.
Parking
Free parking is in the lot behind the building. There are 12 spaces, including 2 close to the side door
for drop-off. The lot is lit until 7:00pm. Please do not park in the delivery lane next to the dumpsters.
Arriving with your dog
Keep your dog on a leash until you are inside the lobby. Please do not let your dog greet other dogs
in the parking lot.

- Daycare reservations: required
- Boarding reservations: required, at least 3 days ahead
- Reserve by phone, website or email

items.question: Can you post my dog's photo on social media?
items.why: A yes or no question answered from page 3 of the PDF.
items.answer: No. We never post a dog's photo on social media without written permission from the owner.

passages.text:
Lost and Found, Photos and Quiet Hours
Lost and found
Items left behind are kept at the front desk for 30 days. Collars, leashes and toys are washed before
they are given back. After 30 days unclaimed items are given to a local rescue.
Photos
Staff take photos for the daily report that goes to owners. We never post a dog's photo on social
media without written permission from the owner.
Quiet hours
During nap time, 12:00pm to 2:30pm, the play yards are closed to visitors so that dogs can rest.
Please avoid dropping by during this time.
Owners receive a daily report with notes on meals, bathroom breaks, and behavior by email. Photos are shared daily.

Owners must send vaccination records from their veterinarian by email address,  in person or by online form. Records must show the dog's name, the vaccine, the date given, and the date it expires. Photos of paper records are not accepted.
Staff can give medications. If we can, owners must provide the medication in its original container with written instructions, and we charge $10 per dose.
